head_commit.message:
[JAX][Mosaic GPU] Disable nvJitLink in GetAssemblyToBinaryCompilationProvider so setmaxnreg is honored (jax-ml/jax#42094)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#42094 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42094), Mosaic GPU kernels compiled through `nvJitLink` ignore `plgpu.set_max_registers` (`ptxas info : (C7504) Potential Performance Loss: 'setmaxnreg' ignored to maintain compatibility across compilation units`), keeping the entry register allocation across all warpgroups and causing severe register spilling on warp-specialized kernels. This happens because `GetAssemblyToBinaryCompilationProvider` in `jaxlib/mosaic/gpu/target.cc` passes `NvJitLinkMode::kAuto`, selecting `NvJitLinkCompilationProvider` when `nvJitLink` is available and `libnvptxcompiler` is not compiled in (such as in the released CUDA wheels).

Solution:
Because Mosaic GPU always compiles a single self-contained PTX module (with `libdevice` and `NVSHMEM` linked as LLVM bitcode prior to PTX emission), change `NvJitLinkMode::kAuto` to `NvJitLinkMode::kDisabled` in `GetAssemblyToBinaryCompilationProvider()` so single-module PTX is compiled whole-program via `libnvptxcompiler` or `ptxas`. Add `CustomCallTest.AssemblyToBinaryCompilationProviderDisablesNvJitLink` in `custom_call_test.cc`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42094

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Avoid overflow and reduce op count in the JVP rule for lax.div.

head_commit.message:
Avoid overflow and reduce op count in the JVP rule for lax.div.

Differentiating `lax.div(x, y)` previously computed `dx / y - x * dy * y**-2`, where `integer_pow[y=-2]` lowers to `1 / (y * y)`. Squaring `y` overflows when `|y|` exceeds `sqrt(maxfloat)` and underflows to zero when `|y|` is smaller than `sqrt(minnormal)`, which can turn finite derivatives into 0 or NaN (via `0 * inf` when `x == 0`). Higher-order derivatives had the same problem with larger powers of `y`.

Rewrite the JVP rule to reuse the primal quotient `q = x / y` and compute the tangent as `(dx - q * dy) / y` (or `q * -(dy / y)` when `dx` is zero, keeping the second division at `y.shape` when `y` is broadcast across `x`). Reusing `q` avoids computing powers of `y` and reduces the emitted op count: joint `(x, y)` forward-mode differentiation drops from 8 HLO ops (3 divisions and 3 multiplies) to 4 (2 divisions and 1 multiply), and joint reverse-mode differentiation drops from 7 HLO ops (3 divisions and 3 multiplies, or 2 divisions and 3 multiplies when the primal quotient is unused and removed as dead code) to 4 (2 divisions and 1 multiply). Only standalone RHS-only `grad` when the primal quotient is unused trades 1 division + 3 multiplies for 2 divisions + 1 multiply in order to avoid squaring `y`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/37909

<details>

<summary>Before and after jaxprs for forward- and reverse-mode differentiation</summary>

`jax.make_jaxpr(lambda x, y, dx, dy: jax.jvp(lax.div, (x, y), (dx, dy)))(x, y, dx, dy)`:

```
# Before (7 eqns; integer_pow[y=-2] lowers to mul + div -> 3 div, 3 mul, 1 neg, 1 add)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[] d:f32[]. let
    e:f32[] = div a b
    f:f32[] = div c b
    g:f32[] = neg d
    h:f32[] = mul g a
    i:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    j:f32[] = mul h i
    k:f32[] = add_any f j
  in (e, k) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 sub)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[] d:f32[]. let
    e:f32[] = div a b
    f:f32[] = mul e d
    g:f32[] = sub c f
    h:f32[] = div g b
  in (e, h) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(lambda x, y, dy: jax.jvp(lambda v: lax.div(x, v), (y,), (dy,)))(x, y, dy)`:

```
# Before (5 eqns -> 2 div, 3 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[]. let
    d:f32[] = div a b
    e:f32[] = neg c
    f:f32[] = mul e a
    g:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    h:f32[] = mul f g
  in (d, h) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[]. let
    d:f32[] = div a b
    e:f32[] = div c b
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = mul d f
  in (d, g) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(jax.grad(lax.div, argnums=(0, 1)))(x, y)`:

```
# Before (6 eqns -> 3 div, 3 mul, 1 neg; `div a b` is dead only if primal is unused)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    _:f32[] = div a b
    c:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    d:f32[] = mul 1.0:f32[] c
    e:f32[] = mul d a
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
  in (g, f) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    c:f32[] = div a b
    d:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
    e:f32[] = neg d
    f:f32[] = mul c e
  in (d, f) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(jax.grad(lax.div, argnums=1))(x, y)`:

```
# Before (5 eqns -> 2 div, 3 mul, 1 neg; `div a b` is dead only if primal is unused)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    _:f32[] = div a b
    c:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    d:f32[] = mul 1.0:f32[] c
    e:f32[] = mul d a
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
  in (f,) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    c:f32[] = div a b
    d:f32[] = mul c 1.0:f32[]
    e:f32[] = neg d
    f:f32[] = div e b
  in (f,) }
```

</details>

display_title: Support 128-lane A scale layout in Mosaic GPU layout inference.

head_commit.message:
Support 128-lane A scale layout in Mosaic GPU layout inference.

On sm_107f, `tcgen05.mma` can read A scale factors from the 128-lane `scales_128_lane_layout()` in TMEM, which avoids duplicating them across the four 32-lane partitions when writing them from registers with `mgpu.async_store_tmem`. Layout inference only ever assigned `scales_layout()` to `a_scale`, so this layout was unreachable from the dialect.

On sm_107f, let `a_scale` take either `scales_layout()` or `scales_128_lane_layout()`; both lower correctly there, and users select the 128-lane one explicitly via `tmem_layout_cast`. On all other architectures keep the fixed `scales_layout()` assignment, so the 128-lane layout can never be inferred and requesting it is reported as unsatisfiable.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Support 128-lane A scale layout in tcgen05 on sm_107f.

head_commit.message:
Support 128-lane A scale layout in tcgen05 on sm_107f.

On `sm_107f`, `tcgen05.mma` supports a 128-lane Scale Factor A (`SFA`) layout in TMEM (enabled via bit 26 of the scaled instruction descriptor). The existing 32-lane layout has to be replicated across all four 32-lane TMEM partitions, so writing A scales from registers via `tcgen05.st` forces every warp to hold and store all 128 rows. With the 128-lane layout, row `r` lives in lane `r`, so each warp writes only its own rows, and the A scales take 4x fewer TMEM columns.

Add `scales_128_lane_layout()` in `tcgen05` (backed by `tmem_default_layout(packing=4)`), accept it for `a_scale` in `mma` on `sm_107f`, and set bit 26 in `_create_scaled_instr_descriptor` when it is used. Collective and sparse MMAs with this layout are rejected for now, since they are not covered by tests yet.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Add lax.fma and lax.fmuladd elementwise fused multiply-add primitives.

head_commit.message:
Add lax.fma and lax.fmuladd elementwise fused multiply-add primitives.

JAX previously lacked elementwise fused multiply-add operations, preventing numerical code and polynomial evaluation from requesting hardware single-rounded multiply-add when available while remaining portable across backends without native FMA support.

Expose two new primitives in `jax.lax` and `jax.extend.core.primitives`:
- `lax.fma(a, b, c)` computes `a * b + c` with single IEEE-754 rounding via `stablehlo.fma` on backends and floating-point types with hardware FMA support.
- `lax.fmuladd(a, b, c)` computes `a * b + c` either as a single-rounded FMA or as `add(mul(a, b), c)`. For floating-point types narrower than 32 bits without native FMA lowering, `fmuladd` may upcast to `float32`, evaluate there, and round back to the input type. On TPU, in forward-compatibility mode, or with older `jaxlib`, it lowers to `add(mul(a, b), c)`.

Bump `jaxlib_extension_version` to 515 to gate `stablehlo.fma` lowering, update `lax.polynomial` (backing `jnp.polyval` and special-function minimax approximations) to evaluate floating-point Horner steps with `lax.fmuladd`, and add `jet`, Mosaic TPU, and Triton GPU rules.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/23919

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

head_commit.message:
Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

Previously, the derivative rule for complex `lax.abs` divided `conj(x)` by `abs(x)`. When `abs(x)` overflowed to infinity for large finite inputs, the gradient collapsed to zero; when one part was much larger than the other, second and higher derivatives lost precision or overflowed `abs(x)**2`; and when one part was ±inf while the other was finite, `inf / inf` produced `NaN` even though the gradient approaches ±1 along the infinite axis.

Compute complex `abs` and its derivative directly from `lax.hypot(real(x), imag(x))`, replacing `NaN` with zero at `0 + 0j` so the gradient there stays `0 + 0j`. In `lax.hypot`, set the infinite axis's component of `(x1 / r, x2 / r)` to `sign(x)` when one argument is ±inf and the other is finite, leaving (±inf, ±inf) and (±inf, NaN) as `NaN`; this also fixes single-axis infinity derivatives for `jnp.hypot` and `jnp.arctan2`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/25681

display_title: Avoid overflow and reduce op count in the JVP rule for lax.div.

head_commit.message:
Avoid overflow and reduce op count in the JVP rule for lax.div.

Differentiating `lax.div(x, y)` previously computed `dx / y - x * dy * y**-2`, where `integer_pow[y=-2]` lowers to `1 / (y * y)`. Squaring `y` overflows when `|y|` exceeds `sqrt(maxfloat)` and underflows to zero when `|y|` is smaller than `sqrt(minnormal)`, which can turn finite derivatives into 0 or NaN (via `0 * inf` when `x == 0`). Higher-order derivatives had the same problem with larger powers of `y`.

Rewrite the JVP rule to reuse the primal quotient `q = x / y` and compute the tangent as `(dx - q * dy) / y`. Reusing `q` avoids computing powers of `y` and reduces the emitted op count: joint `(x, y)` forward-mode differentiation drops from 8 HLO ops (3 divisions and 3 multiplies) to 4 (2 divisions and 1 multiply), and joint reverse-mode differentiation drops from 7 HLO ops (3 divisions and 3 multiplies, or 2 divisions and 3 multiplies when the primal quotient is unused and removed as dead code) to 4 (2 divisions and 1 multiply). Only standalone RHS-only `grad` when the primal quotient is unused trades 1 division + 3 multiplies for 2 divisions + 1 multiply in order to avoid squaring `y`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/37909

<details>

<summary>Before and after jaxprs for forward- and reverse-mode differentiation</summary>

`jax.make_jaxpr(lambda x, y, dx, dy: jax.jvp(lax.div, (x, y), (dx, dy)))(x, y, dx, dy)`:

```
# Before (7 eqns; integer_pow[y=-2] lowers to mul + div -> 3 div, 3 mul, 1 neg, 1 add)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[] d:f32[]. let
    e:f32[] = div a b
    f:f32[] = div c b
    g:f32[] = neg d
    h:f32[] = mul g a
    i:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    j:f32[] = mul h i
    k:f32[] = add_any f j
  in (e, k) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 sub)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[] d:f32[]. let
    e:f32[] = div a b
    f:f32[] = mul e d
    g:f32[] = sub c f
    h:f32[] = div g b
  in (e, h) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(lambda x, y, dy: jax.jvp(lambda v: lax.div(x, v), (y,), (dy,)))(x, y, dy)`:

```
# Before (5 eqns -> 2 div, 3 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[]. let
    d:f32[] = div a b
    e:f32[] = neg c
    f:f32[] = mul e a
    g:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    h:f32[] = mul f g
  in (d, h) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[] c:f32[]. let
    d:f32[] = div a b
    e:f32[] = mul d c
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = div f b
  in (d, g) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(jax.grad(lax.div, argnums=(0, 1)))(x, y)`:

```
# Before (6 eqns -> 3 div, 3 mul, 1 neg; `div a b` is dead only if primal is unused)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    _:f32[] = div a b
    c:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    d:f32[] = mul 1.0:f32[] c
    e:f32[] = mul d a
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
  in (g, f) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    c:f32[] = div a b
    d:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
    e:f32[] = neg d
    f:f32[] = mul c e
  in (d, f) }
```

`jax.make_jaxpr(jax.grad(lax.div, argnums=1))(x, y)`:

```
# Before (5 eqns -> 2 div, 3 mul, 1 neg; `div a b` is dead only if primal is unused)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    _:f32[] = div a b
    c:f32[] = integer_pow[y=-2] b
    d:f32[] = mul 1.0:f32[] c
    e:f32[] = mul d a
    f:f32[] = neg e
    g:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
  in (f,) }

# After (4 eqns -> 2 div, 1 mul, 1 neg)
{ lambda ; a:f32[] b:f32[]. let
    c:f32[] = div a b
    d:f32[] = div 1.0:f32[] b
    e:f32[] = neg d
    f:f32[] = mul c e
  in (f,) }
```

</details>

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [AutoPGLE] Let the host run ahead and enqueue work

head_commit.message:
[AutoPGLE] Let the host run ahead and enqueue work

In the steady state, the host usually runs ahead of the devices and
queues work long before it executes, hiding some host-side overheads.
When profiling for PGLE, the profiled executable is usually submitted
onto an empty device, which can let those host-side overheads bleed into
the measured costs. Launch a small delay kernel (default: 25ms) before
the device-side barrier that was already introduced. This can also be
used by applications that programatically trigger profiling of the
latter stages of their execution via jax.profiler or cudaProfilerStart
to clean up the start of those profiles.

Enable multihost_utils_test on GPU in OSS, the baseline passes on GPU
with a fix to gpu::GpuExecutableRunOptions::set_incarnations in xLA.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

head_commit.message:
Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

Previously, the derivative rule for complex `lax.abs` divided `conj(x)` by `abs(x)`. When `abs(x)` overflowed to infinity for large finite inputs, the gradient collapsed to zero; when one part was much larger than the other, second and higher derivatives lost precision or overflowed `abs(x)**2`; and when one part was ±inf while the other was finite, `inf / inf` produced `NaN` even though the gradient approaches ±1 along the infinite axis.

Compute complex `abs` and its derivative directly from `lax.hypot(real(x), imag(x))`, replacing `NaN` with zero at `0 + 0j` so the gradient there stays `0 + 0j`. In `lax.hypot`, set the infinite axis's component of `(x1 / r, x2 / r)` to `sign(x)` when one argument is ±inf and the other is finite, leaving (±inf, ±inf) and (±inf, NaN) as `NaN`; this also fixes single-axis infinity derivatives for `jnp.hypot` and `jnp.arctan2`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/25681

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Improve accuracy and reduce op count of jax.lax.erfc.

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy and reduce op count of jax.lax.erfc.

Previously, `erfc` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` approximated `erfcx(|x|)` in `1 / |x|`. Because `1 / |x|` blows up near `0`, it needed a separate `1 - erf(x)` polynomial for `|x| < 1`, three or four more polynomial pieces across `|x| >= 1`, and two divisions, with `select`s to pick between them (`chlo.erfc`, used for `bfloat16`, similarly evaluates three interval polynomials and two divisions). In vector code every polynomial runs on every input, so most of that work is thrown away.

Shifting the reciprocal to `u = 1 / (|x| + c)` (`c = 2` for `bfloat16` and `float32`, `c = 4` for `float64`) maps all `|x| >= 0` onto `(0, 1/c]` without blowing up at `0`, so a single polynomial `erfc(|x|) = exp(-x^2) * u * P(u)` covers all `x >= 0` (with `2 - erfc(|x|)` for `x < 0`) using one reciprocal and no interval splits.

Enable this new implementation for `float32` and `float64` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, and for `bfloat16` in all accuracy modes: on `bfloat16`, both `chlo.erfc` and the new implementation are correctly rounded (`<= 0.5` ULP) and bitwise identical on every non-NaN `bfloat16` input across CPU, GPU, and TPU (and both return NaN on NaN inputs), while cutting the StableHLO op count from 63 to 25.

StableHLO operation counts (after expanding `chlo.erfc` and running CSE, excluding constants) and worst-case ULP errors:

| Implementation | Add/Sub/Neg | Mul | Div | Exp | Compare/Select | Other | Total Ops | Max ULP |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `bfloat16` before (`chlo.erfc`) | 24 | 25 | 2 | 1 | 8 | 3 | 63 | 0.5 |
| `bfloat16` after (default & `HIGHEST`) | 9 | 9 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 25 | 0.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` before | 43 | 40 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 105 | 4.0–5.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` after | 44 | 35 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 6 | 88 | 1.5 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` before | 84 | 80 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 186 | 2.5–3.0 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` after | 79 | 53 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 12 | 147 | 2.0 |

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy and reduce op count of jax.lax.erfc.

Previously, `erfc` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` approximated `erfcx(|x|)` in `1 / |x|`. Because `1 / |x|` blows up near `0`, it needed a separate `1 - erf(x)` polynomial for `|x| < 1`, three or four more polynomial pieces across `|x| >= 1`, and two divisions, with `select`s to pick between them (`chlo.erfc`, used for `bfloat16`, similarly evaluates three interval polynomials and two divisions). In vector code every polynomial runs on every input, so most of that work is thrown away.

Shifting the reciprocal to `u = 1 / (|x| + c)` (`c = 2` for `bfloat16` and `float32`, `c = 4` for `float64`) maps all `|x| >= 0` onto `(0, 1/c]` without blowing up at `0`, so a single polynomial `erfc(|x|) = exp(-x^2) * u * P(u)` covers all `x >= 0` (with `2 - erfc(|x|)` for `x < 0`) using one reciprocal and no interval splits.

Enable this new implementation for `float32` and `float64` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, and for `bfloat16` in all accuracy modes: on `bfloat16`, both `chlo.erfc` and the new implementation are correctly rounded (`<= 0.5` ULP) and bitwise identical on every non-NaN `bfloat16` input across CPU, GPU, and TPU (and both return NaN on NaN inputs), while cutting the StableHLO op count from 63 to 25.

StableHLO operation counts (after expanding `chlo.erfc` and running CSE, excluding constants) and worst-case ULP errors:

| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `bfloat16` before (`chlo.erfc`) | 24 | 25 | 2 | 1 | 8 | 3 | 63 | 0.5 |
| `bfloat16` after (default & `HIGHEST`) | 9 | 9 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 25 | 0.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` before | 43 | 40 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 105 | 4.0–5.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` after | 44 | 35 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 6 | 88 | 1.5 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` before | 84 | 80 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 186 | 2.5–3.0 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` after | 79 | 53 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 12 | 147 | 2.0 |

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

head_commit.message:
Fix complex abs derivatives across overflow, cancellation, and infinity.

Previously, the derivative rule for complex `lax.abs` divided `conj(x)` by `abs(x)`. When `abs(x)` overflowed to infinity for large finite inputs, the gradient collapsed to zero; when one part was much larger than the other, second and higher derivatives lost precision or overflowed `abs(x)**2`; and when one part was ±inf while the other was finite, `inf / inf` produced `NaN` even though the gradient approaches ±1 along the infinite axis.

Compute complex `abs` and its derivative directly from `lax.hypot(real(x), imag(x))`, replacing `NaN` with zero at `0 + 0j` so the gradient there stays `0 + 0j`. In `lax.hypot`, set the infinite axis's component of `(x1 / r, x2 / r)` to `sign(x)` when one argument is ±inf and the other is finite, leaving (±inf, ±inf) and (±inf, NaN) as `NaN`; this also fixes single-axis infinity derivatives for `jnp.hypot` and `jnp.arctan2`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/25681

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma on SM103.

On SM103 (`sm_103a`, GB300), dense 4-bit block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` (`mxf4` and `mxf4nvf4`) supports `K=96` (48 bytes per MMA step) in addition to `K=64` (32 bytes per MMA step), reducing the number of MMA instructions required per K tile by up to 1.5×.

Infer `K=96` support in `tcgen05.mma` when `utils.get_arch() == utils.Arch(10, 3)` for dense 4-bit block-scaled SMEM operands with 128B swizzle. Encode SM103 SMEM descriptors with bit 52 set (absolute address mode for LBO) so 48B steps can cross 128B swizzle atom boundaries into the next K tile, and set bit 31 and sub-word scale factor IDs in `_create_scaled_instr_descriptor`. Decompose K tiles with `K % 64 == 0` into `96*a + 64*b` (`b` in 0, 1, or 2), placing `K=64` tail steps at 32B/128B-aligned offsets so they never cross a swizzle atom boundary.

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy and reduce op count of jax.lax.erfc.

Previously, `erfc` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` approximated `erfcx(|x|)` in `1 / |x|`. Because `1 / |x|` blows up near `0`, it needed a separate `1 - erf(x)` polynomial for `|x| < 1`, three or four more polynomial pieces across `|x| >= 1`, and two divisions, with `select`s to pick between them (`chlo.erfc`, used for `bfloat16`, similarly evaluates three interval polynomials and two divisions). In vector code every polynomial runs on every input, so most of that work is thrown away.

Shifting the reciprocal to `u = 1 / (|x| + c)` (`c = 2` for `bfloat16` and `float32`, `c = 4` for `float64`) maps all `|x| >= 0` onto `(0, 1/c]` without blowing up at `0`, so a single polynomial `erfc(|x|) = exp(-x^2) * u * P(u)` covers all `x >= 0` (with `2 - erfc(|x|)` for `x < 0`) using one reciprocal and no interval splits.

Enable this new implementation for `float32` and `float64` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, and for `bfloat16` in all accuracy modes: on `bfloat16`, both `chlo.erfc` and the new implementation are correctly rounded (`<= 0.5` ULP) and bitwise identical on every non-NaN `bfloat16` input across CPU, GPU, and TPU (and both return NaN on NaN inputs), while cutting the StableHLO op count from 63 to 25.

| `bfloat16` after (default & `HIGHEST`) | 9 | 9 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 25 | 0.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` before | 43 | 40 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 105 | 4.0–5.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` after | 44 | 35 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 6 | 88 | 1.5 |

head_commit.message:

With check_vma=True and jax_auto_pcast=False, `all_gather(x, axis,
to='invarying')` accepted an `x` invariant over `axis`, and differentiating it
then failed in the backward pass with an internal `dynamic_slice` error. Now

all_gather, so this raises while tracing. Forward-only uses now raise too, as
with `to='varying'`; use `jax.lax.pcast(x, axis, to='varying')` instead.

display_title: Fix nested shard_map axis selection under vmap in Explicit mode. Also…

head_commit.message:
Fix nested shard_map axis selection under vmap in Explicit mode. Also error out if there are no mesh axes left to go Manual over.

When `jax.vmap` maps over an `Explicit` mesh axis, `shard_map`'s batching rule removes that axis from `explicit_mesh_axis_names` before binding on the parent trace without restoring it while tracing the batched body. A nested `shard_map` inside that body then treats the vmapped `Explicit` axis as eligible to become `Manual`, rather than excluding it. In addition, `shard_map` previously allowed the resolved manual axis set to become empty after subtracting already-manual mesh axes.

Re-enter `add_explicit_mesh_axis_names` while tracing the batched `shard_map` body so nested `shard_map` calls continue excluding vmapped `Explicit` axes.

Partially addresses https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42058.

display_title: Fix nested shard_map axis selection under vmap in Explicit mode. Also error out if there are no mesh axes left to go Manual over.

head_commit.message:
Fix nested shard_map axis selection under vmap in Explicit mode. Also error out if there are no mesh axes left to go Manual over.

When `jax.vmap` maps over an `Explicit` mesh axis, `shard_map`'s batching rule removes that axis from `explicit_mesh_axis_names` before binding on the parent trace without restoring it while tracing the batched body. A nested `shard_map` inside that body then treats the vmapped `Explicit` axis as eligible to become `Manual`, rather than excluding it. In addition, `shard_map` previously allowed the resolved manual axis set to become empty after subtracting already-manual mesh axes.

Re-enter `add_explicit_mesh_axis_names` while tracing the batched `shard_map` body so nested `shard_map` calls continue excluding vmapped `Explicit` axes.

Partially addresses https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42058.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix lax.pmean and constant lax.psum for uneven axis_index_groups.

head_commit.message:
Fix lax.pmean and constant lax.psum for uneven axis_index_groups.

When `axis_index_groups` contains groups of different sizes, `lax.pmean` previously divided every group's sum by the size of the first group (`len(axis_index_groups[0])`). This happened because `lax.pmean` computes the per-group denominator via `_axis_size(axis_name, axis_index_groups)` (which calls `psum(1, axis_name, axis_index_groups=axis_index_groups)`), and `_psum` took its constant-folding fast path whenever the input had no tracers, multiplying the constant by `len(axis_index_groups[0])` across all devices.

Restrict the constant-folding fast path in `_psum` to cases where `axis_index_groups` is `None` or all groups in `axis_index_groups` have the same length, falling back to binding `psum_p` when group sizes vary so each replica group computes its own sum. Also preserve `weak_type` on the output abstract value in `_allreduce_effectful_abstract_eval` so that `psum(1, ...)` retains a weak integer type when bound as a primitive.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41132

display_title: Fix lax.pmean and constant lax.psum for uneven axis_index_groups.

head_commit.message:
Fix lax.pmean and constant lax.psum for uneven axis_index_groups.

When `axis_index_groups` contains groups of different sizes, `lax.pmean` previously divided every group's sum by the size of the first group (`len(axis_index_groups[0])`). This happened because `lax.pmean` computes the per-group denominator via `_axis_size(axis_name, axis_index_groups)` (which calls `psum(1, axis_name, axis_index_groups=axis_index_groups)`), and `_psum` took its constant-folding fast path whenever the input had no tracers, multiplying the constant by `len(axis_index_groups[0])` across all devices.

Restrict the constant-folding fast path in `_psum` to cases where `axis_index_groups` is `None` or all groups in `axis_index_groups` have the same length, falling back to binding `psum_p` when group sizes vary so each replica group computes its own sum. Also preserve `weak_type` on the output abstract value in `_allreduce_effectful_abstract_eval` so that `psum(1, ...)` retains a weak integer type when bound as a primitive.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41132

head_commit.message:
Reduce per-call C++ dispatch overhead on jit and pjit cache hits.

On C++ `jit` and `pjit` cache hits, `PjitFunction::Call` previously inspected `PyArray` arguments across separate passes and built intermediate containers that are not needed in the common case.

display_title: [shard_map] Require all collective axes to be present in the input's …

head_commit.message:
[shard_map] Require all collective axes to be present in the input's varying/unreduced/reduced set

Several collective abstract-eval rules only checked that the requested axes
*overlapped* the input's manual axis types (non-empty intersection). That let
through cases where only some of the axes were varying, unreduced or reduced,
which produced wrong output types. These rules now check that the requested
axes are a *subset* of the matching set:

  * psum_invariant (axes vs. varying)
  * all_gather_reduced (axis_name vs. varying)
  * unreduced_psum_scatter (axis_name vs. unreduced)
  * unreduced_psum / pmax / pmin (axes vs. unreduced)
  * vary_unreduced_cast (axes vs. varying)
  * reduced_vary_cast (axes vs. reduced)

Also:
  * Reject integer axes before the membership check in psum_invariant and
    unreduced_psum/pmax/pmin, so users get the clearer error.
  * psum_invariant's error messages now use the calling primitive's name
    (still `psum` for psum_invariant), and the unneeded `named_axes`
    filtering is gone.
  * Add a shard_map test covering partial axis overlap in
    `all_gather(..., to='reduced')` (the other five rules sit behind
    `_get_from` on the public API).
  * Remove the follow-up disjointness checks between `varying` and
    `reduced`/`unreduced`: `ManualAxisType` enforces that `varying` is disjoint
    from both `unreduced` and `reduced`, so once `axes` is checked with
    `issubset`, it cannot overlap the opposing set.

display_title: Improve float32 precision of jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf

head_commit.message:
Improve float32 precision of jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf

Previously, `jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf` computed the log-combinatorial term via `gammaln(y + n) - gammaln(n) - gammaln(y + 1)` and the `(1 - p)**y` term via `xlogy(y, 1 - p)`. In `float32`, subtracting large `gammaln` values causes catastrophic cancellation when `n >> y` or `y >> n`, and forming `1 - p` loses precision when `p` is small.

Compute the combinatorial term as `-betaln(n, y) - log(y)` for `y > 0` (and `0` for `y == 0`), and use `xlog1py(y, -p)` in place of `xlogy(y, 1 - p)` to match `scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42145

head_commit.message:
Improve implementation of `jax.scipy.special.betaln`.

Re-implement `jax.scipy.special.betaln` in `jax/_src/scipy/betaln.py` (removing `jax/_src/third_party/scipy/betaln.py`) with improved numerical accuracy across extreme argument ratios, negative non-integer and integer inputs, and non-finite boundaries. Also use `lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` for `lax.log1p` in `jax.scipy.stats.t.logpdf` to avoid catastrophic cancellation in float32 on TPU.

- Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38243
- Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39106

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Fix ROCm/oneAPI `static_libcxx` and CUDA 13 `ci_linux_x86_64_cuda13` `.bazelrc` configs

After switching `common:linux` in `.bazelrc` to `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:stdlib=libc++` and `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:static_libcxx=true`:

1. `common:rocm_clang_hermetic` in `build/rocm/rocm.bazelrc` and `common:oneapi` in `.bazelrc` override `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:stdlib=libstdc++`, which requires also setting `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:static_libcxx=False` (matching XLA's `tensorflow.bazelrc`) so `rules_ml_toolchain` does not attempt to link static `libc++` when `stdlib=libstdc++` is selected.
2. In `.bazelrc`, the comment `# Use NVCC for CUDA 13 builds since CUDA 13.4 nvcc supports libc++.` was followed by a typo (`common:ci_linux_x86_64_cuda12 --config=build_cuda_with_nvcc` instead of `common:ci_linux_x86_64_cuda13 --config=build_cuda_with_nvcc`), which overrode `common:ci_linux_x86_64_cuda12 --config=build_cuda_with_clang` back to `nvcc` on CUDA 12 CI builds and left `ci_linux_x86_64_cuda13` without `--config=build_cuda_with_nvcc`.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Improve float32 precision of jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf

head_commit.message:
Improve float32 precision of jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf

Previously, `jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf` computed the log-combinatorial term via `gammaln(y + n) - gammaln(n) - gammaln(y + 1)` and the `(1 - p)**y` term via `xlogy(y, 1 - p)`. In `float32`, subtracting large `gammaln` values causes catastrophic cancellation when `n >> y` or `y >> n`, and forming `1 - p` loses precision when `p` is small.

Compute the combinatorial term as `-betaln(n, y) - log(y)` for `y > 0` (and `0` for `y == 0`), and use `xlog1py(y, -p)` in place of `xlogy(y, 1 - p)` to match `scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42145

display_title: [Pallas] Include axis and mesh context in Mosaic lowering cache key.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas] Include axis and mesh context in Mosaic lowering cache key.

`PallasLoweringCacheKey` included `grid_sizes` and `grid_arity` but omitted `grid_names`, `core_axis_names`, and `jax_mesh_context`. When two `pallas_call` kernels in the same lowered module shared the same grid dimensions with different axis names (such as `(('x', 2), ('y', 2))` and `(('y', 2), ('x', 2))`), `lax.axis_index('x')` collided in `pallas_lowering_cache` and reused the wrong grid index in the second kernel. DMA and semaphore lowering rules that translate device IDs also depend on `core_axis_names` and `jax_mesh_context`.

Add `grid_names`, `core_axis_names`, and `jax_mesh_context` to `PallasLoweringCacheKey` and populate them in `jaxpr_subcomp` so cached equation lowerings stay isolated across distinct axis and mesh contexts.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [remat3] fix Ref reads and writes under jax.remat

head_commit.message:
[remat3] save Ref reads instead of re-reading them in the backward pass

The remat3 backward pass recomputed Ref reads, but by then the Ref may have
been written, by the rematted function itself or by later code, so the
recomputation saw the wrong values. Save each get or swap result from the
forward pass as a residual, and use PrimalLeftTangentRight so the recomputed
read still carries the Ref's tangent. This means Ref reads under remat3 are
always saved, whatever the policy.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Pallas:TPU] Zero-extend 16-bit top_k indices to int32

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Zero-extend 16-bit top_k indices to int32

In `_top_k_impl`, `lax.argmax` on `bfloat16` inputs returns 16-bit indices, and
the reduced dimension may have up to 2^16 elements, so the indices are unsigned.
Cast via `uint16` before widening to `int32` so the conversion lowers to
`arith.extui` instead of `arith.extsi`, which previously sign-extended indices >= 32768 into negative values.
